findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database volume, snapshots and automated backups store all data unencrypted. Any access to the underlying storage or a shared snapshot exposes cleartext data.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet (the endpoint is also exported as an output). This places a credential-only authentication boundary directly on the public internet and defeats network segmentation for the data tier.

The user_data script interpolates var.password and the DB username into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc in cleartext. EC2 user data is retrievable by anyone able to reach the instance metadata service (including via SSRF from the PHP application) and by any principal with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking the database master password.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the web server. This violates least privilege and gives any compromise of the instance the ability to read/delete all S3 data, manipulate all EC2 infrastructure, and modify or snapshot every RDS instance in the account.

No metadata_options block is set, so the instance permits IMDSv1 token-less metadata requests. Combined with the internet-facing PHP application and the wildcard instance-profile policy, a single SSRF gives an attacker the role's temporary credentials.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's root volume, which contains the plaintext dbinfo.inc credential file, may be stored unencrypted.

The parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, and the application connects with mysqli_connect() without TLS options, so database traffic including credentials can traverse the network in cleartext.
The security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained data-exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the database security group.
Port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR rather than to the web tier's security group, so every workload in the VPC can reach the database directly, widening lateral-movement paths.
The master username is hard-coded to the well-known value "admin", which combined with the public endpoint makes credential-guessing attacks against the database materially easier.
